name: John Dewey
epithet: Democracy as a way of living
dossier: American philosopher and educator. Democracy and Education (1916), The Public and Its Problems (1927), and Human Nature and Conduct (1922) are quoted here; all three are in the public domain in the United States. Later books, including Liberalism and Social Action (1935), are still in copyright and are not quoted.
voice: I ask whether this is a shared life, or only a machine for decisions.

works.title: The Public and Its Problems
works.note: 1927. Public domain in the United States. Project Gutenberg.

entries.claim: A democracy is more than a form of government; it is primarily a mode of associated living, of conjoint communicated experience.
entries.loc: Chapter 7, The democratic conception in education
entries.bears: Democracy, here, is a way of living and communicating, not only a ballot.

entries.claim: Society exists through a process of transmission quite as much as biological life.
entries.loc: Chapter 1, Education as a necessity of life
entries.bears: A society continues by passing on habits, ideas, and standards.

entries.claim: Men live in a community in virtue of the things which they have in common; and communication is the way in which they come to possess things in common.
entries.loc: Chapter 1, Education as a necessity of life
entries.bears: What people hold in common, and how they communicate it, is what makes a community.

entries.claim: Results, conduct, are what counts; they afford the sole measure of morality.
entries.bears: He measures morality by conduct and results, not by a named intuition.

entries.claim: The only statement which can be made is a purely formal one: the state is the organization of the public effected through officials for the protection of the interests shared by its members.
entries.bears: The state is not, for him, a thing apart from a public and its officials.

entries.claim: No government by experts in which the masses do not have the chance to inform the experts as to their needs can be anything but an oligarchy managed in the interests of the few.
entries.bears: Expertise does not replace a public that can tell the experts what it needs.

entries.claim: Viewed as a historical tendency exhibited in a chain of movements which have affected the forms of government over almost the entire globe during the last century and a half, democracy is a complex affair.
entries.bears: He refuses to treat democracy as one simple machine.

entries.claim: Customs in any case constitute moral standards. For they are active demands for certain ways of acting.
entries.bears: A moral standard, here, is a custom that demands a way of acting, not a rule delivered from outside the habits people already share.
